source.title: From Collapse to Stability: A Knowledge-Driven Ensemble Framework for Scaling Up Click-Through Rate Prediction Models
source.authors: Hong-Hao Li; Lei Sang; Yi Zhang; Guangming Cui; Yi-Wen Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some plotted figures and parts of the extracted text are garbled, but the relevant findings are also stated in the text or tables.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling trends in CTR prediction ensembles, a setting beyond language-model pretraining, and reports how outcomes vary with ensemble size, method, and dataset.
record.gate_note: The paper measures CTR AUC and Logloss while varying the number of ensemble sub-networks. This is not a language-model parameter/token/compute sweep, and it does not fit power laws or find a compute-optimal parameter/token split. Rows below capture its reported CTR scaling results as evidence for the cross-setting and curve-shape aspects only. Scaling-law results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is a CTR-ensemble method paper. It invokes Kaplan-style scaling laws as motivation and measures AUC as the number of sub-networks grows from 1x to 10x. Table VII shows total parameters only rise from 15.71M (2x) to 20.30M (10x) because embeddings dominate, so there is no multi-order-of-magnitude sweep. No loss power law is fitted, and the measure is AUC on ensemble count, not loss against parameters, data or compute. Most of the scaling results (KD, DML, KDEF) report the authors' own method against mean fusion. The finding that mean-fusion ensembles degrade with sub-network count is a related but different construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim that KD lets CTR ensembles 'follow scaling laws' and that KDEF yields an 'ensemble scaling law'. These claims rest on monotone AUC gains over 1x–10x sub-networks, with no power-law fit.
record.recipe_differences: Studies CTR prediction ensembles, varying sub-network count and measuring AUC/Logloss; it does not use the original language-model loss, size, data, or compute scaling procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with fusion/training method (mean, sum, concat, KD, DML, KDEF) and dataset (Criteo versus KKBox); the authors report possible overfitting on the relatively smaller KKBox dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: In CTR models, adding parallel sub-networks with mean, sum or concat fusion lowers ensemble AUC and sharply lowers sub-network AUC. Examples: MLP 81.39 to 81.25 and FINAL 81.44 to 81.23 at 10x on Criteo. Knowledge-transfer training (KDEF) makes AUC rise modestly instead (e.g. MLP 81.39 to 81.60).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Widening CTR models by ensembling more jointly trained sub-networks does not improve performance unless knowledge transfer between sub-networks is added.

record.problems: The scaling experiments report CTR AUC rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy. Scaling is measured by sub-network count, not parameter count, training tokens, or compute. No power-law fits, uncertainty estimates for the scaling curves, or compute-optimal allocation are reported; several plotted numerical series are not reliably extractable from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 2, 4, 6, and 8 contain additional scale-by-scale plotted values, but the extracted plot labels and values are garbled. Table II has many model-by-dataset-by-scale entries; only values explicitly used in the paper's scaling discussion were retained.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss and no parameter, token or compute sweep.
No fits on small runs and no extrapolation.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit in the CTR setting, and the parameter range is far below orders of magnitude.
No downstream prediction from scale or loss.
No exponents or fitting choices are compared.

missing.what: Parameter counts per ensemble size: 15.71M at 2x to 20.30M at 10x. The sweep spans only ~1.3x in parameters, with KDEF Logloss 0.4368 to 0.4360.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 and V7 links and labels are dropped. The scaling axis is ensemble sub-network count with a small change in total parameters, the measure is AUC, and most rows compare the authors' KDEF method with baselines. Mentions of Kaplan et al. are motivation and citation only.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss or parameter, token, or compute sweep.
No small-run fits or extrapolation to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and training tokens.
Does not vary depth or width at a fixed parameter count to test their effect on loss.
Tests CTR ensemble performance as sub-network count changes, not power-law fit quality in other modalities or the listed regimes such as repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream task performance prediction from pretraining loss or scale.
Reports dataset- and method-dependent scaling trends, including non-monotonic results, but does not estimate exponents, compare fitting methods, or test compute-optimal allocation.

rows.subject: MLP ensemble
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of sub-networks using mean, sum, and concatenation fusion; reported ensemble AUC trends.
rows.value: Performance gradually decreases as the number of sub-networks increases, regardless of fusion method; sum and concat are more unstable than mean.
rows.locator: Section IV-A1, Fig. 2(a) and accompanying text
rows.note: Trend stated in text; plotted numeric values are not reliably extractable.
rows.check: Measures AUC against ensemble sub-network count over a ~1.3x parameter range, not loss on a power-law scale. Table II MLP mean fusion gives 81.39 (base) to 81.36 (6x) to 81.25 (10x), a small decline that should be cited with numbers.

rows.subject: MLP sub-networks
rows.operation_detail: Varied ensemble size and reported best- and worst-performing individual sub-network AUC trends.
rows.measure: Individual sub-network AUC and best–worst variation
rows.value: Sub-network performance declines more sharply as the ensemble grows, with substantial variance between the best and worst sub-networks.
rows.locator: Section IV-A1, Fig. 2(b) and accompanying text
rows.note: The paper reports the trend explicitly; no numerical series is stated in the text.
rows.check: Measures individual sub-network AUC inside an ensemble, not the scaled model's loss. Table II MLP Meanb drops from 80.42 (2x) to 74.49 (10x).

rows.subject: MLP ensemble with knowledge distillation
rows.operation_detail: Used the mean ensemble prediction as an abstract teacher and varied the number of sub-networks.
rows.measure: Ensemble AUC and individual sub-network AUC
rows.value: The paper reports that KD makes ensemble performance improve with increasing parameters and moderately reduces sub-network performance decline and variance.
rows.locator: Section IV-B, Figs. 4(a)–(b) and accompanying text
rows.note: The paper describes the trend as following scaling laws, but does not fit or report a power-law curve.
rows.check: Compares the authors' KD variant with plain fusion (own method versus baseline). The 'follows scaling laws' wording is the authors'; no curve or fit is reported.

rows.subject: MLP ensemble with deep mutual learning
rows.operation_detail: Added peer-to-peer mutual learning among sub-networks and varied ensemble size.
rows.measure: Ensemble AUC and individual sub-network AUC
rows.value: DML does not address the ensemble-performance degradation reported for ordinary fusion, but reduces sub-network decline and variance and narrows the gap between a sub-network and the ensemble.
rows.locator: Section IV-C, Figs. 5(b) and 6 and accompanying text
rows.note: The DML comparison is reported as qualitative trends; plotted numerical values are not reliably extractable.
rows.check: Compares the DML variant with the baseline (method comparison). The rate of scaling is not measured.

rows.subject: KDEF ensemble
rows.size_stated: 2x–6x sub-networks in Fig. 8; the paper also reports 10x results
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of sub-networks using the combined KD, DML, and examination mechanism framework.
rows.value: The KDEF ensemble is reported to outperform the KD and DML ensembles consistently as sub-network count increases.
rows.locator: Section IV-E, Fig. 8(a) and accompanying text
rows.note: The text describes a stable improvement, but does not establish that the trend follows a power law.
rows.check: Compares KDEF with KD and DML (own method versus others), not a scaling-law test. The baseline is other methods, not a smaller scale.

rows.subject: FINAL ensemble using mean fusion
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean-fusion ensemble performance at 10x scale with the independently trained base model.
rows.baseline: 81.44 for the independently trained FINAL model
rows.note: The paper gives the comparison in the text and table.
rows.check: FINAL mean fusion: 81.44 (base) to 81.23 (10x). The value is correct, but this is ensemble-count scaling with a small parameter increase, not a version's construct.

rows.subject: FINAL ensemble using KDEF
rows.operation_detail: Compared KDEF ensemble performance at 10x scale with the independently trained base model.
rows.baseline: 81.44 for the independently trained FINAL model
rows.note: Improvement with scale is reported, but the study does not fit a power law.
rows.check: Own-method result (KDEF 81.62 at 10x against 81.44 base). This is a method-performance row.

rows.subject: PNN ensemble using KDEF
rows.operation_detail: Reported the KDEF ensemble result at 10x scale.
rows.baseline: 85.07 for the independently trained PNN model
rows.note: The text states this exceeds mean fusion by more than 0.001; no power-law fit is reported.
rows.check: Own-method result (KDEF PNN 85.45 at 10x against 85.07 base on KKBox). This is a method-performance row.

rows.subject: KDEF CTR ensembles
rows.operation_detail: Compared KDEF scaling outcomes across datasets and ensemble sizes.
rows.value: Models on KKBox do not always achieve their best performance at 10x; the authors attribute this in part to limited data and overfitting.
rows.note: The text states the dataset-dependent non-monotonic trend; it does not specify a single model or give an aggregate value for this statement.
rows.check: There is no baseline value, and the statement aggregates several models. It reports non-monotonic KDEF AUC on KKBox (e.g. FINAL KDEF peaks at 5x, 85.68, then 85.48 at 10x). It is not an exponent or fit-dependence result, so its V7 link is wrong.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CTR ensemble scaling in the tested fusion and training setups
reader_labels.reason: Ordinary fusion degrades as sub-network count grows (r1–r2), while KD and KDEF produce different trends (r3, r5–r8); the study does not establish a common power-law form.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that performance does not always peak at 10x and links this to dataset size and overfitting, consistent with a curve that can depart from a simple monotonic trend (r9).
